answer: To cross the trust bridge, each entity anchors its identity in cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. Validating new identities requires staking bonding curves: each concurrent node inside a malicious cluster demands superlinear collateral, creating exponential capital exhaustion for Sybil swarms. Rather than drowning the network in an ocean of clones, attackers face escalating costs where cultivating a fake grove of agents becomes mathematically ruinous.
